Closes #2918 

#### Motivation and Context
The `Volatility` getter was throwing the following error:
```
Cannot convert type 'Python.Runtime.PyObject' to 'decimal'
```

issue_context.title: Conversion error in VolatilityModelPythonWrapper.Volatility
issue_context.body:
#### Expected Behavior
The `Volatility` getter in `VolatilityModelPythonWrapper` should not throw exceptions

#### Actual Behavior
The `Volatility` getter in `VolatilityModelPythonWrapper` throws the following error in some cases:
```
Microsoft.CSharp.RuntimeBinder.RuntimeBinderException: Cannot convert type 'Python.Runtime.PyObject' to 'decimal'
  at (wrapper dynamic-method) System.Object.CallSite.Target(System.Runtime.CompilerServices.Closure, System.Runtime.CompilerServices.CallSite, object)
  at (wrapper delegate-invoke) .invoke_bound_Decimal_Closure_CallSite_object(System.Runtime.CompilerServices.CallSite, object)
  at QuantConnect.Python.VolatilityModelPythonWrapper.get_Volatility () [0x00097] in :0 
  at QuantConnect.Algorithm.Framework.Alphas.Analysis.Providers.AlgorithmSecurityValuesProvider.GetValues (QuantConnect.Symbol symbol) [0x00052] in :0 
  at QuantConnect.Algorithm.Framework.Alphas.Analysis.SecurityValuesProviderExtensions.GetValues (QuantConnect.Algorithm.Framework.Alphas.Analysis.ISecurityValuesProvider securityValuesProvider, System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable`1[T] symbols) [0x0001e] in :0 
```

#### Potential Solution
The cause is floating point precision in the new implementation of Python decimals.
The solution is to cast the `PyObject` to `double` before casting to `decimal`.

#### Reproducing the Problem
The same error can be repeated with this example:
``` C#
var input = 0.00008954686015144748m;
dynamic obj = ConvertToPyObject(input);
var result = (decimal)obj;
```
The last line will throw the same exception.

#### Checklist
- [x] I have completely filled out this template
- [x] I have confirmed that this issue exists on the current `master` branch
- [x] I have confirmed that this is not a duplicate issue by searching [issues](https://github.com/QuantConnect/Lean/issues)
- [x] I have provided detailed steps to reproduce the issue

review_comments: Using `NumberStyles.Number | NumberStyles.AllowExponent` in the PythonNet converter seems to solve the issue too https://github.com/QuantConnect/pythonnet/blob/master/src/runtime/converter.cs#L944 . The issue triggers when the `string` representation uses the exponent format. I think it might be better to change the converter directly so it covers any other use case too
